ai.title: Inject git status and diff into project file context
ai.summary: System prompt now includes git status, diff, and cached diff via ProjectFileContext. Backend getRelevantFilesPromptPart2 renders <git_status>, <git_diff>, <git_diff_cached> tags when gitChanges present. npm-app/src/project-files.ts executes git commands via child_process.exec, caching results in ProjectFileContextSchema. common/src/util/file.ts adds gitChanges field to ProjectFileContextSchema; fileTree uses z.custom<FileTreeNode>() instead of FileTreeNodeSchema. Git command failures return empty strings, silently omitting git context from prompt.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant about your project, it now quietly reads your in-progress file edits and recently staged changes from Git, then feeds that real-time context directly into its reply. This only affects you if you're running the project locally with Git tracking enabled, and if Git reports no changes or isn't available, the assistant simply omits that extra detail without any error.

ai.title: Inject recent git commit messages into system prompt
ai.summary: Added `git_commit_messages_most_recent_first` block to system prompt. Mechanism: `getGitChanges` executes `git shortlog HEAD~100..HEAD`, parses output, and reverses order to ensure most recent commits appear first. Scope: `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` template, `common/src/util/file.ts` schema, `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` logic. Detail: `ProjectFileContextSchema` updated with `lastCommitMessages` string field; fallback to empty string on error.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant about the most recent 100 changes made to your project, and it will know what was just worked on without you having to paste the history. When you open a session, the assistant's instructions automatically include a list of the latest git commit messages, so it can reference your recent work and respond in context. This applies to anyone using the tool on a project tracked with git, and it works as soon as you start a new session today.
